habitat: Small flocks in broad-leaved woodland, mixed bushveld and thornveld, feeding in large trees.
summary: A common resident. A green parrot with a brown head and yellow eyes. The body is pale green and the wings are dark green. In flight the back is apple-green and the underwing coverts are yellow. The immature is duller than the adult. Newman does not print a call phrase. The Kemp paper name Brownheaded Parrot and the code RB were left unchanged.

similar.note: Meyer’s Parrot has a yellow bar on the forehead and yellow shoulders. Its upper parts are described as grey-brown, not the pale green body of Brown-headed Parrot.

research.note: Newman calls it a common resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. Newman does not print a call phrase. The immature is only described as duller. No flight photograph shows the apple-green back or the yellow underwing. The grade A call is from Satara Camp. Population figures and the Kemp name Brownheaded Parrot were left unchanged.
